Prerequisite: A server certificate issued by the DoD PKI (or another approved CA) for the FortiAuthenticator services, with its private key
What it enables: DoD-issued certificates for the GUI (HTTPS), the EAP server, RADSEC, the LDAP service, the SAML IdP, and the FortiClient SSO Mobility Agent service
How to put it in place: Create a server certificate with Issuer Third-party CA to generate a CSR and have the CA sign it, or import a signed certificate; GUI: Certificate Management > End Entities > Local Services (Create New or Import)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "End entities" (server certificates, Issuer Third-party CA generates a CSR to be signed by a third-party CA; "To import a server certificate") and "FortiAuthenticator unit configuration" under "Port-based network access control" (create a server certificate before configuring EAP)

Prerequisite: The DoD root and intermediate CA certificates (and the CA certificate of any other server FortiAuthenticator connects to over TLS) imported as trusted CAs
What it enables: Validation of the certificates of remote LDAP servers, syslog servers, SCIM servers, RADSEC clients, and EAP-TLS supplicants, and certificate bindings to a DoD issuing CA
How to put it in place: Obtain the CA certificates from the PKI; GUI: Certificate Management > Certificate Authorities > Trusted CAs (Import, or Learn Certificate from a server)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Trusted CAs" (no third-party trusted CA certificates are preinstalled), "LDAP" (Secure Connection, CA Certificate), "Syslog servers" (Trusted certificate), "Service providers" under "SCIM" (the SCIM server CA certificate must be imported in the Trusted CAs), and "Configuring certificates for EAP"

Prerequisite: Current revocation data for every CA in the chain: a CRL from the CA's CRL distribution point, imported or downloaded automatically, or a reachable OCSP responder
What it enables: Revocation checking of EAP-TLS client certificates (CRL, or OCSP from 8.0.2) and of remote LDAP server certificates (CRL Check Mode, from 8.0.0)
How to put it in place: Download the most recent CRL from a CDP listed in the certificate; GUI: Certificate Management > Certificate Authorities > CRLs (Import); for OCSP, make the PKI's OCSP responder reachable from FortiAuthenticator
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Certificate revocations lists" (To import a CRL), "LDAP" (CRL Check Mode All Nodes: a CRL must be configured for every CA in the chain), and "Auth profiles" (OCSP verification modes; the OCSP timeout is fixed at 3 seconds)

Prerequisite: A remote LDAP directory (such as Microsoft Active Directory or OpenLDAP) that offers LDAPS or STARTTLS, with a bind account that can search the base DN
What it enables: Remote LDAP users and administrators, remote user synchronization rules, and Windows AD domain authentication
How to put it in place: Create the bind account in the directory; GUI: Authentication > Remote Auth. Servers > LDAP (Primary server name/IP, Base distinguished name, Bind Type, Secure Connection)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "LDAP" under "Remote authentication servers" and "Remote user sync rules- LDAP" (the rules work only with LDAP servers whose group memberships can be retrieved from a user object's attribute, for example the memberof overlay on OpenLDAP)

Prerequisite: A Windows AD user account with at least domain user privileges and the delegated right to manage computer objects, plus the domain's Kerberos realm and NetBIOS names
What it enables: Joining FortiAuthenticator to the AD domain for PEAP-MSCHAPv2 (Windows Active Directory Domain Authentication)
How to put it in place: Create the minimum-privilege account in Active Directory and delegate the management of computer objects to it; GUI: Authentication > Remote Auth. Servers > LDAP (Windows Active Directory Domain Authentication: Kerberos realm name, Domain NetBIOS name, Administrator username)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "LDAP" (Windows Active Directory Domain Authentication) and "Configure minimum privilege Windows AD user account"

Prerequisite: A remote RADIUS server that accepts FortiAuthenticator as a client, with a shared secret
What it enables: Remote RADIUS users and RADIUS proxying to an existing server
How to put it in place: Add FortiAuthenticator as a client on the remote RADIUS server; GUI: Authentication > Remote Auth. Servers > RADIUS
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "RADIUS" under "Remote authentication servers"

Prerequisite: A remote TACACS+ server that accepts FortiAuthenticator, with a shared secret (and a second server for redundancy)
What it enables: Remote TACACS+ authentication and the optional secondary server
How to put it in place: Add FortiAuthenticator on the remote TACACS+ server; GUI: Authentication > Remote Auth. Servers > TACACS+
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "TACACS+" under "Remote authentication servers"

Prerequisite: A remote SAML identity provider, with its metadata or certificate, that can return the MFA authentication context
What it enables: Remote SAML users and the MFA authentication context
How to put it in place: Obtain the IdP metadata or certificate from the identity provider; GUI: Authentication > Remote Auth. Servers > SAML (Import IDP metadata/certificate)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "SAML" under "Remote authentication servers"

Prerequisite: A Device FQDN for FortiAuthenticator, resolvable by the users' browsers
What it enables: The SAML IdP portal and its IdP URLs
How to put it in place: Add the name to DNS; GUI: System > Dashboard > Status (System Information widget, Device FQDN)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "General" under "SAML IdP" (to configure the Device FQDN setting, a Device FQDN must be entered in the System Information widget) and "System information widget"

Prerequisite: SAML service providers configured with the FortiAuthenticator IdP metadata, and their SP metadata (entity ID and ACS URL)
What it enables: SAML service provider entries, token-based authentication for each SP, and authorization of users for each SP
How to put it in place: Load the IdP metadata downloaded from FortiAuthenticator on each SP; GUI: Authentication > SAML IdP > Service Providers (Import SP metadata)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Service providers" under "SAML IdP" (IdP metadata, Import SP metadata; the IdP address must first be configured under SAML IdP General)

Prerequisite: FortiToken hardware tokens or FortiToken Mobile licenses, registered on FortiAuthenticator over a valid FortiGuard connection (FortiToken Mobile activation needs an online connection to fortitokenmobile.fortinet.com, also in offline provisioning mode)
What it enables: One-time password authentication with FortiToken and FortiToken Mobile for administrators and users, and the RADIUS, TACACS+, LDAP, SAML IdP, and portal features that use it
How to put it in place: Purchase the tokens or FortiToken Mobile licenses; GUI: System > Administration > FortiGuard (FortiToken Hardware Provisioning and FortiToken Mobile Provisioning servers reachable); GUI: Authentication > User Management > FortiTokens (Create New or Import)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring One-Time Password (OTP) authentication" (FortiToken and FortiToken Mobile tokens must first be registered), "FortiAuthenticator and FortiTokens" (registration needs a valid FortiGuard connection; a seed file for air-gapped networks), "FortiToken Mobile licenses", "Tokens" (Offline provision mode), and "Licensing" (FTM licenses are purchased separately)

Prerequisite: A FortiIdentity Cloud (formerly FortiToken Cloud) account with the users' tokens
What it enables: One-time passwords from FortiIdentity Cloud tokens
How to put it in place: Provision the users in FortiIdentity Cloud; GUI: Authentication > User Management > Local Users (One-Time Password (OTP) authentication, token source FortiIdentity Cloud)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring One-Time Password (OTP) authentication" (token source FortiAuthenticator or FortiIdentity Cloud); the LDAP, RADIUS, TACACS+, OAuth, and SAML servers do not support password and OTP concatenation for FortiIdentity Cloud-issued FortiToken Mobile tokens

Prerequisite: FIDO security keys for the users, and browsers that support FIDO registration and authentication
What it enables: FIDO authentication for user accounts, FIDO user verification, and FIDO logins to the SAML IdP
How to put it in place: Issue FIDO keys to the users; GUI: Authentication > User Management > Local Users (FIDO authentication, Register FIDO key)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Local users" (FIDO authentication, Register FIDO key) and "Tokens" (FIDO user verification instructs the end user's browser)

Prerequisite: An external SMTP mail relay for the organization's domain, with STARTTLS and an account if it requires authentication
What it enables: Email from FortiAuthenticator: one-time passwords, notifications, and certificate expiry warnings
How to put it in place: Set up the relay to accept mail from FortiAuthenticator; GUI: System > Messaging > SMTP Servers (Create New, Secure connection STARTTLS, Enable authentication); GUI: System > Messaging > Email Services
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Messaging" and "SMTP servers" (the built-in mail server is not recommended; relay email from an official mail server) and "Policies" under "Certificate management" (Send a warning email)

Prerequisite: Network devices configured as RADIUS or TACACS+ clients of FortiAuthenticator: its address, the same shared secret, and the authentication port, with Message-Authenticator, RADSEC, and EAP support where the rows use them, and for RADSEC from 8.0.3 a client certificate from a CA in the trusted CAs (P2)
What it enables: RADIUS and TACACS+ clients, the Message-Authenticator requirement, RADSEC, and RADIUS accounting over RADSEC
How to put it in place: Configure each switch, wireless controller, firewall, or other network device with FortiAuthenticator as its RADIUS or TACACS+ server (the configuration depends on the vendor)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring switches and wireless controllers to use 802.1X authentication" (RADIUS server IP, key, and authentication port 1812) and "TACACS+ service" (Adding clients); FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Release Notes, "Special notices" (Mutual authentication required for RADSec connections: RADSec clients must authenticate with a trusted client certificate); FortiAuthenticator 8.0 Ports (RADSEC TCP/2083)

Prerequisite: Client certificates for EAP-TLS and EAP-TEAP on the users' devices, issued by a CA that FortiAuthenticator trusts (for example DoD PKI or PIV certificates), with the MAC address in the CN where it is verified
What it enables: EAP-TLS and EAP-TEAP authentication, certificate bindings, and the MAC address check in the client certificate
How to put it in place: Issue the certificates from the PKI or from a FortiAuthenticator local CA through SCEP, and install them on the supplicants (outside FortiAuthenticator)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "FortiAuthenticator and EAP" (certificate management and SCEP for device certificates) and "Auth profiles" (Client Credential Certificates, Verify MAC address in CN of client certificate)

Prerequisite: Remote syslog servers (two for redundancy) that accept syslog over TLS, with a server certificate signed by a CA that FortiAuthenticator trusts and, from 8.0.3, a valid hostname
What it enables: Off-loading of the audit records to a central log server over TLS
How to put it in place: Set up the syslog servers; GUI: Logging > Log Config > Syslog Servers (Secure Connection Enable, Trusted certificate)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Syslog servers" (up to 20 servers; TLS with a CA or trusted certificate to verify the server certificate) and "Log settings"; FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Release Notes, "Special notices" (Using remote syslog servers with Secure connection enabled: without a server certificate with a valid hostname, the TLS connection fails)

Prerequisite: A FortiAnalyzer or FortiManager unit that accepts logs from FortiAuthenticator
What it enables: Off-loading of the audit records to FortiAnalyzer or FortiManager
How to put it in place: Add FortiAuthenticator as a device on the FortiAnalyzer or FortiManager; GUI: Logging > Log Config > Log Settings (Send logs to FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer with its IP address)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Log settings" (To configure logging to a FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer unit)

Prerequisite: An SFTP server (and a secondary server) with an account and a directory for FortiAuthenticator
What it enables: Remote log backups and configuration auto-backups
How to put it in place: Create the account and directory on the SFTP server; GUI: System > Administration > FTP Servers (Connection type SFTP, Username, Password)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "FTP servers", "Log settings" (select an FTP server for log backups), and "Configuring auto-backup"

Prerequisite: An SNMP manager that supports SNMP v3, loaded with the Fortinet and FortiAuthenticator MIB files
What it enables: SNMP v3 monitoring and SNMP traps
How to put it in place: Load the MIBs on the SNMP manager; GUI: System > Administration > SNMP (SNMP v3 users with the manager as a host)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "SNMP" (the manager must be listed as a host; it needs the Fortinet and FortiAuthenticator MIB files)

Prerequisite: Two NTP servers (DoD time sources), with the authentication key number, type, and value where NTP authentication is used
What it enables: Accurate time stamps and time synchronization
How to put it in place: Obtain the NTP server addresses and keys; GUI: System > Dashboard > Status (System Information widget, System Time, NTP enabled)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring the system date, time, and time zone" (NTP server 1 and 2, Enable authentication with a key number, type, and value)

Prerequisite: A second FortiAuthenticator of the same model and licensing mode, with the same firmware version, its own license of the same size, and a Layer 2 link for the HA interface (a crossover cable is preferred)
What it enables: The active-passive HA cluster and the separate heartbeat interface
How to put it in place: License the second unit (a VM license is tied to an IP address that is the same on both units or unique to the HA interface), connect the HA interfaces, and upgrade both units to the same firmware; GUI: System > Administration > Licensing; GUI: System > Administration > High Availability (Role Cluster member on each unit)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "High availability" (Layer 2 connectivity is mandatory; same firmware version and same sized license; License compatibility and HA deployment scenarios: active-passive nodes must use the same model and licensing mode) and "Licensing" (Licensing FortiAuthenticator HA units)

Prerequisite: Load-balancer FortiAuthenticator units, each with a user license large enough to replicate the configuration from the standalone primary
What it enables: Load-balancing HA
How to put it in place: License each load balancer; GUI: System > Administration > Licensing; GUI: System > Administration > High Availability (Role Load Balancer)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Licensing" (HA load-balancer license size) and "High availability" (up to ten load balancers; LB nodes can differ in model and licensing mode)

Prerequisite: A SafeNet Luna v7 network HSM with an SSH administrator account and a key partition, which authorizes FortiAuthenticator as a client
What it enables: Storage of local CA private keys on an HSM
How to put it in place: Configure the HSM, then upload the FortiAuthenticator client certificate to it; GUI: System > Administration > NetHSMs
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "NetHSMs" (Safenet Luna v7 is the only supported HSM type; configure an SSH administrator account and key partition first)

Prerequisite: A ZTNA server (for example a FortiGate access proxy) in front of the remote LDAP servers, and a client certificate that authenticates FortiAuthenticator to it
What it enables: Zero trust tunnels to remote LDAP servers
How to put it in place: Set up the ZTNA server, then create the tunnel with the client certificate; GUI: System > Network > Zero Trust Tunnels (URL, Client certificate)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Zero trust tunnels" (URL of the ZTNA server and a client certificate; the remote zero trust server setup is in the FortiAuthenticator Cookbook)

Prerequisite: A SCIM service provider with its SCIM endpoint and access token, and its CA certificate in the trusted CAs (P2)
What it enables: SCIM provisioning of users to service providers
How to put it in place: Obtain the endpoint and access token from the service provider; GUI: Authentication > SCIM > Service Provider (SCIM endpoint, Access token)
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Service providers" under "SCIM" (the SCIM server CA certificate must be imported in the Trusted CAs)

Prerequisite: A SCIM client (an upstream identity provider such as Microsoft Entra ID) with an account that has the needed SCIM permissions, and a FortiAuthenticator administrator API key
What it enables: Remote user synchronization pushed over SCIM
How to put it in place: Configure the SCIM client with the FortiAuthenticator SCIM base URL and an administrator's API key; GUI: Authentication > User Management > Remote User Sync Rules
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Remote user sync rules- SCIM" (Prerequisites: a SCIM client account with the appropriate permissions and an administrator with the Administrator role to generate an API key)

Prerequisite: A FortiClient SSO Mobility Agent (SSOMA) license for the number of SSOMA clients
What it enables: FSSO with FortiClient SSO Mobility Agent clients
How to put it in place: Purchase the SSOMA license and upload it; GUI: System > Administration > Licensing
Source: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Licensing" (FortiAuthenticator licenses: maximum number of SSO Mobility Agent clients; SSOMA, FTM, and SMS licenses are purchased separately; a subscription VM includes an add-on SSOMA entitlement in its license file)
